record.prBody:
## New breaking API major 2026-09-30.endive; callers must review breaking items before pinning or upgrading (SDK/webhook endpoints too) [Needs review]

### Change

The repo stays on its explicit `2025-11-17.clover` pin and stripe-node v20. I did not bump the pin or the SDK. I reviewed the Endive breaking items against every Stripe call site and found one real hit: `payment_method_types: ['card']` in `createCheckoutSession` (lib/billing/stripe.ts, around line 98). That call was missing from the inventory's field list. Endive removes the parameter from Checkout Session create, and a request that includes it returns a 400. The only code change is a comment at that line with the exact replacement to use. No runtime behavior changed. The other call sites are unaffected: `customers.create`, the `billingPortal` session, `subscriptions` cancel, update and retrieve (it reads `items.data[0].id`, not the removed `current_period_*`), `coupons.create`, and the webhook `constructEvent`. The webhook handler's event types are unaffected too, and webhook endpoints keep their own configured `api_version`.

Files touched:
- `lib/billing/stripe.ts`

### Why

Endive is a new breaking Stripe API major, and stripe-node v23+ pins it. Moving to it without a change would make Checkout Session creation fail with a 400. The replacement, `allowed_payment_method_types`, doesn't exist on clover. So swapping it now would break the live pin, and the fix has to land together with the version or SDK bump.

> As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | fail (283) | fail (283) | 0 |
| build | fail (1) | fail (1) | 0 |
| test | fail (204) | fail (205) | 1 |

New failures: 1

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `stripe__stripe_api_versions`: pass
- `stripe__stripe_check_params`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- stripe__stripe_api_versions: pass (Listed 39 breaking entries from clover to endive, crossing dahlia and endive. Only the Checkout `payment_method_types` removal touches this repo.)
- stripe__stripe_check_params: fail (POST /v1/checkout/sessions with apiVersion 2026-09-30.endive flagged `payment_method_types` as unknown and suggested `allowed_payment_method_types`. That is the expected result for the current code, which is valid on the clover pin. I did not change the call, so it will fail on Endive until the follow-up below.)

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy

### Unproven

- I did not run run_checks after the edit. The baseline typecheck, build and test were already failing, and a comment cannot change their results.
- I did not test against the live Stripe API or in test mode.
- I did not check the Dashboard payment-method settings or each webhook endpoint's configured api_version.
- I did not check whether `allowed_payment_method_types` type-checks in stripe-node v23+, since v23 isn't installed.
- typecheck was already failing before the change and still fails.
- build was already failing before the change and still fails.
- test: new failure `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'findMany')`
- test was already failing before the change and still fails.
- Validator stripe__stripe_check_params failed: Spec: live stripe/openapi tag v2596, the last spec whose info.version was 2026-09-30.endive: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/openapi/v2596/openapi/spec3.json (info.version 2026-09-30.endive).

### Behaviour changes

- None at runtime. The only edit is a comment in lib/billing/stripe.ts.
- Follow-up before moving the pin or upgrading to stripe-node v23+: replace `payment_method_types: ['card']` with `allowed_payment_method_types: ['card']`, which keeps card-only. Alternatively, drop the parameter to use dynamic payment methods, which can offer more payment methods than card.

---

# Removes the payment method types parameter from Checkout Sessions

## What’s new

Removes the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) parameter from the [create Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) method. You can no longer pass `payment_method_types` when you create a Checkout Session. Use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) to manage payment methods from the Dashboard without writing code.

You can also use [excluded_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-excluded_payment_method_types) to exclude specific payment methods from the dynamic payment methods results or the new [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types) parameter to specify a set of payment methods.

The [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types)  parameter accepts an array of payment method type and filters the list to only compatible payment methods based on other parameters such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. The compatible subset is shown in the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#checkout_session_object-payment_method_types) property of the response.

Previously, [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-08-26.dahlia#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) returned an error when you specified an incompatible payment method. `allowed_payment_method_types` silently filters out incompatible methods and returns only those that work with the current configuration.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Passing `payment_method_types` as a parameter when you [create a Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) now returns a `400` error. If your integration sets this parameter, you must remove it and migrate to [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types).

## Impact

This migration requires careful attention if your integration passes `payment_method_types` when creating a Checkout Session. You must update your integration to use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or switch to `allowed_payment_method_types` to get automatic compatibility filtering instead of errors. Requests that include `payment_method_types` on this now return a `400` error.

# Removes the payment method types parameter from Checkout Sessions

## What’s new

Removes the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) parameter from the [create Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) method. You can no longer pass `payment_method_types` when you create a Checkout Session. Use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) to manage payment methods from the Dashboard without writing code.

You can also use [excluded_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-excluded_payment_method_types) to exclude specific payment methods from the dynamic payment methods results or the new [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types) parameter to specify a set of payment methods.

The [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types)  parameter accepts an array of payment method type and filters the list to only compatible payment methods based on other parameters such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. The compatible subset is shown in the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#checkout_session_object-payment_method_types) property of the response.

Previously, [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-08-26.dahlia#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) returned an error when you specified an incompatible payment method. `allowed_payment_method_types` silently filters out incompatible methods and returns only those that work with the current configuration.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Passing `payment_method_types` as a parameter when you [create a Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) now returns a `400` error. If your integration sets this parameter, you must remove it and migrate to [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types).

## Impact

This migration requires careful attention if your integration passes `payment_method_types` when creating a Checkout Session. You must update your integration to use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or switch to `allowed_payment_method_types` to get automatic compatibility filtering instead of errors. Requests that include `payment_method_types` on this now return a `400` error.
